description: Core's hillside grading carrier, its pads (NF.H3, first slice; core ADR-0001 §§1–5, §8): the grading plan of a World IR (pads, terraces and retaining walls, the walls between neighbours, the report, the findings) and its point function. Cases carry §9's cases 1, 2, 3, 4, 9, 10 and 11; the stairs (§6, cases 5–8) are the next slice.

contract.reportLine: N grading patches not applied (only when N > 0)
contract.overlapSlopeRule: On the world lattice (i, j) × overlapSlopeLatticeM, a point covered (padFlatOutside < reach) by two or more of the plan's pads, at least one a hillside pad, is read: the point function's gradient (dividers included) by central differences of overlapSlopeDiffM, only when the four difference points lie in the same grading part of every covering pad and on the same side of every divider. A slope over standMaxGradient + overlapSlopeTolerance charges every pair of its covering pads of which at least one is a hillside pad (a hillside pad and a default pad included; two default pads never). Charged pairs are divided by neighbourWallRule; each pair still charged after that is one finding "pads <id> and <id>: where their grading regions overlap, the graded ground off the walls is steeper than <standMaxDeg>°", pairs ascending by id, after the pads' own findings.
contract.neighbourWallRule: Walls between neighbours (§5): each pair overlapSlopeRule charges on the blended ground, taken ascending by id, is divided by a straight retaining wall. The candidate lines are separating lines of the two lots (fit rectangles): for each axis (the lower id's away and across axes, the other's, then the centre-to-centre axis; each oriented from the lower id's centre toward the other's, a square axis as given; an axis the same as an earlier kept one, or along which the lots overlap by more than 1e-9 m, left out) the line square to it at the middle of the gap between the lots' projections, widest gap first, axis order on a tie: one wall on each such line first (stripHalfM 0), then, for each line whose gap is over 1e-9 m and in the same order, a shared terrace filling the gap (stripHalfM half the gap). With s the signed distance past the line toward the other pad and h = stripHalfM, the lower id grades only s < h and the other only s >= -h (a pad on its far side is left out of the blend); on the shared terrace -h <= s < h the ground is the mean of the two blends, each with one of the pair left out. A default member is sized as a hillside pad. The first candidate is kept with which no dividing wall (of any division) steps over wallMaxM; if none is kept the pair stays blended and any promotion is undone. Each pair is tried once; the rule is read again on the divided ground until it charges no untried pair. A dividing wall is wall.<lower id>.nb.<other sourceFeatureId>.<n> (a shared terrace's edges .nb.<other>.1.<n> at s = -h and .nb.<other>.2.<n> at s = h): each line sampled across both pads' reach boxes at most gradedCellM apart (both ends), top and base read 1e-6 m either side; a pad's own wall line does not step past its dividing line, and is cut there 1e-4 m inside (on the arc, on a corner's arc).
contract.frame: Metres in core's relative frame over [0, terrainSize]²: an IR point p is the frame point p + terrainSize / 2; a height is n × verticalScale.value of the bilinear heightmap, nothing added.

replay.input: Each case's world is a World IR cut down to what the plan reads. For each engine in engines, build the grading plan; evaluate the point function at each of points, with otherPads (GradeLots' pads of the world's non-map lots, core TerrainPad shape) in the same pad set; and, when otherPads is given, check that set for a map lot stacked on GradeLots.
replay.compare: A refusal compares refused only. Otherwise pads, walls (every vertex), report, findings, points and padSet, numbers within tolerance (metres; awayX, awayZ and carryM within tolerance.unit), the rest exactly, object key sets included.
replay.controls: Each control is a case's answer with one thing changed. A checker must refuse every one: compare it with what the engine answers, and check the answer's own invariants (no wall vertex over wallMaxM; the report counts the pads and prints its line only when there are some; no wall on a default pad).

cases.name: interior-and-edge-points
cases.note: Clear flat area: the centre, the fit rectangle's and the flat area's corners are at the target; the band's middle (2 m out, smoothstep weight 0.5) is raw + 0.5 × (target − raw); its outer edge (4 m out) and beyond are raw.

cases.name: default-parity-with-gradedheight
cases.note: Two gentle map lots (one turned 30°, one an L fitted on its minimum rectangle) with a street: both default pads, so every graded height is gradedHeight over the plan's pads (and gradeTerrain's grid at its nodes).

cases.name: cross-engine-pad-heights
cases.note: One IR fragment every engine replays: its pad ids (pad.map.<sourceFeatureId>), target heights and the patch count. The lot footprint and the dressed ground surface make no pad. elevation is stated, so every engine projects alike.

cases.name: terraced-pad
cases.note: A 12 × 8 m lot on a 20 % slope (11.3°, under standMaxDeg) running 28.6° off its axes: a hillside pad. Its clear flat area is at the target, every step is a wall of at most WALL_MAX_M, no slope outside the walls exceeds standMaxDeg, and the ground beyond the band is raw (pinned densely by hillside-corpus.test.ts).

cases.name: report-line-for-a-map-world
cases.note: Three map buildings: three patches, and the line "3 grading patches not applied".

cases.name: no-map-world-has-an-empty-plan
cases.note: No map-derived record: no pad, no wall, no report line, the ground raw. computePlacement and computeGeographyPlacement of this world are byte-identical to core main (hillside-corpus.test.ts).

cases.name: one-pass-with-gradelots-pads
cases.note: §3: the plan's pads plus GradeLots' pad of a non-map lot, one pass: padSet is null and each lot is graded once.

cases.name: a-pad-stacked-on-gradelots-is-refused
cases.note: §3: GradeLots' pad of the map lot itself beside the plan's pad: padSet is the refusal (the map lot graded twice).

expected.padSet: map lot footprint.map.fp-gentle is graded by core's pad pad.map.fp-gentle and stacked on a GradeLots pad (footprint.map.fp-gentle)

cases.name: overlapping-neighbours-16m
cases.note: ADR §2's example: A at 0 m and B at 1 m, 5 m half-widths, 16 m apart. Where B's band reaches A's flat area the ground is gradedHeight's weighted mean (0.135 m at 6 m, 0.333 m at 7 m), not A's target; where no other band reaches, it is the target.

points.label: A's clear flat area (5 m from A's centre, away from B)

cases.name: overlapping-neighbours-14m
cases.note: The variant with B 14 m away: A's fit-rectangle corner nearest B is 0.333 m (B's band, 2 m out, weight 0.5); a building on A seats on that ground by BYOA B7, an engine's fit, not a value core states.

points.label: A's fit corner farthest from B
A's fit corner farthest from B

cases.name: terraced-neighbours
cases.note: Terraced houses side by side on a hill: two hillside pads whose terraces and bands overlap. gradedHeight's blend would tilt the ground between them past standMaxDeg, so a retaining wall divides them (wall.pad.map.a.nb.b.1, on x = 32 between the lots) and each pad grades only its own side: every slope off the walls is within standMaxDeg and there is no finding (pinned densely by hillside-corpus.test.ts). The same pair 30 m apart does not overlap and is not divided (hillside-grading.test.ts).

cases.name: terraced-house-and-default-shed
cases.note: A terraced house with a shed flush beside it on a hill: the shed is a default pad by §5's trigger, and their grading regions overlap. gradedHeight's blend would tilt the ground off the walls past standMaxDeg, so a retaining wall divides them on the lots' shared edge (wall.pad.map.a.nb.b.1, the 1.35 m between the two targets) and the shed is graded as a hillside pad: every slope off the walls is within standMaxDeg and there is no finding. Two overlapping default pads are never divided (§2 parity; hillside-grading.test.ts).

cases.name: terraced-house-and-shed-across-a-gap
cases.note: A terraced house and a shed 2 m beyond it on a hill, their targets 1.6 m apart: one wall between them would step over WALL_MAX_M, so the gap between the lots (x from 34 to 36) is a shared terrace, the mean of the two sides' ground, with a wall on each edge (wall.pad.map.a.nb.b.1.1 and wall.pad.map.a.nb.b.2.1) taking half the step; the shed is graded as a hillside pad. Every slope off the walls holds and there is no finding.

points.label: the shared terrace, between the lots
the shared terrace, between the lots

cases.name: terraced-house-and-lean-to-undividable
cases.note: A terraced house and a lean-to (a default pad alone) whose lots overlap along every axis: no separating line exists, so no wall can divide them. The pair stays blended, the lean-to a default pad, and the blend's slope off the walls where they overlap is over standMaxDeg, so the answer carries the overlap finding naming both pads (the never-silent guard; pinned densely by hillside-corpus.test.ts).

findings: pads pad.map.a and pad.map.b: where their grading regions overlap, the graded ground off the walls is steeper than 15°

cases.name: terraced-house-and-flush-shed-over-the-wall-limit
cases.note: A terraced house and a shed (a default pad alone) flush beside it, their targets 1.54 m apart: the one candidate dividing wall would step over WALL_MAX_M, so the division is refused and the shed's promotion undone. The shed stays a default pad with no walls, the pair stays blended, and the answer carries the overlap finding naming both pads (the never-silent guard).

findings: pads pad.map.a and pad.map.b: where their grading regions overlap, the graded ground off the walls is steeper than 15°

cases.name: flush-staggered-neighbours-over-the-wall-limit
cases.note: Two terraced houses flush side by side and staggered up the hill, their targets 1.92 m apart: every dividing wall on a candidate line would step over WALL_MAX_M, so the pair stays blended (no nb walls, no promotion) and the answer carries the overlap finding naming both pads (the never-silent guard).

findings: pads pad.map.a and pad.map.b: where their grading regions overlap, the graded ground off the walls is steeper than 15°
